pages_reviewed.page_title: Trailer Repairs | Indianapolis, Indiana | Paul's Trailer Service Inc.
pages_reviewed.visible_content: Homepage describes the company as family-owned and operating since 1978, outlines trailer repair and parts, gives weekday hours, and prominently provides phone and email contact.
Lists common repair and inspection services, trailer types served, hourly labor rates, and estimate terms.

pages_reviewed.page_title: Trailer Parts | Indianapolis, Indiana | Paul's Trailer Service Inc.
pages_reviewed.visible_content: Describes OEM and aftermarket parts availability, installation, and an extensive set of manufacturer and parts-brand listings.
Provides the Indianapolis street address, phone numbers, fax, email, and map/directions links.

pages_reviewed.page_title: Trailer Storage and Leasing | Indianapolis, Indiana
pages_reviewed.visible_content: Describes short- and long-term parking for equipment, rates, gate access hours, and weekend/holiday limitations.

business_facts: Paul's Trailer Service says it was founded in 1978 and serves the greater Indianapolis area, with a customer base extending across North America.
The listed services include brakes, suspension, electrical work, welding, ABS diagnostics, DOT inspections, trailer alignment, and structural repairs.
The company says it services a wide variety of trailer types, but excludes reefer units and tires.
The parts page describes OEM and aftermarket replacement parts and offers installation; it says some parts may be in stock or available within 1–2 days.
The listed location is 1245 Harding Court, Indianapolis, Indiana 46217. Contact details include 317-781-9212, 800-792-3451, and paulstrailers@sbcglobal.net.
The homepage lists weekday hours as 8 AM to midnight.

evidence: The site addresses trailer repair, parts, inspections, and equipment parking, and lists a broad range of trailer types.
The site displays local contact details and a toll-free number, plus location and directions.
inference: Likely audiences include commercial fleet operators, owner-operators, and other trailer owners seeking repair, parts, inspection, or parking.
The primary conversion path appears to be calling the business; email and visiting the location are secondary paths.
